idiom_name: hand-written frame validation with a second POSIX message queue as the invalid channel
implementation_notes: C has no runtime type system and no reflective decoder, so the validation step is explicit - length, framing header, version and checksum before any interpretation - and the invalid channel is a second mqd_t opened with mq_open: the receiver calls mq_send on the error queue with the original bytes and a reason code, then continues with the next frame. POSIX message queues give the invalid channel its own bounded depth and priority range; a ZeroMQ pair (or PUSH to an error consumer) is the distributed equivalent and is reachable from every other language. The classic structure is worth keeping here precisely because there is no safety net: the invalid channel is the only thing that stops a corrupt frame from being read as a valid one.
pitfalls: mq_receive overwrites its buffer on the next call, so the frame must be copied (or owned by the queue) before it is forwarded; otherwise the invalid channel receives mixed or truncated bytes.
mq_send blocks when the error queue is full; use O_NONBLOCK or mq_timedsend plus a documented overflow policy, or the receiver hangs on its own error path.
POSIX queues accept zero-length messages, so an explicit size check is required - a length of 0 is not a success signal.
